solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Steady progress? Judge wrong turning outside sporting blunder

indicators.note: whatever is outside wraps around something else, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: J is the standard abbreviation for judge
OG is an own goal, the classic football blunder

indicators.note: something turning faces the other way, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: A referee's bad call and a sporting howler hardly amount to steady progress for a team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judge wrong' looks like a verb phrase about a bad decision, but they are separate pieces; a tort is a civil wrong in law.
explanation.definitionFit: A jog-trot is a slow, regular running pace, hence figuratively plodding, steady advance.

clue.text: Unemployed girl getting word from well-wisher?

parts.note: Jo is a common short girl's name
'Bless you!' is what a kindly person says, so the word offered is this one

explanation.surface: An out-of-work young woman receives a kind message from someone wishing her well.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the well-wisher's word is only one example of what they might say: 'bless'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a person without paid work; they are straightforward synonyms.

clue.text: Exploitation of gasfield annoying people

indicators.note: exploiting a resource means working it over and changing it, so the letters get reworked

parts.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Drilling a gas field upsets people, a familiar environmental complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a news report about fracking protests; 'Exploitation of' is the signal to rearrange the single word that follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A gadfly is literally a biting insect and figuratively a person who persistently irritates or provokes others.

clue.text: Son au naturel, perhaps, got up

indicators.note: someone au naturel is wearing nothing, so here one letter is dressed only in a word for nothing

parts.note: the French phrase points to French, where the word for nothing is this one
S is the standard abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A naked boy leaps out of bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Au naturel means naked, wearing nothing; since the phrase is French, the nothing is French too: RIEN, worn around S to give RI-S-EN.
explanation.definitionFit: Risen is the past participle of rise, meaning stood or climbed up, matching got up as a verb form.

clue.text: Salesman with top drawer, see, concealed in counter

indicators.note: what is concealed in something sits inside it, so these pieces go within another

parts.note: a teller counts money, for example in a bank
a Royal Academician is an artist of the highest rank, a top drawer in the sense of someone who draws
v, short for Latin vide, means see in references

explanation.surface: A salesman shows off a high-quality chest of drawers hidden behind a shop counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top drawer' pretends to mean posh or a piece of furniture, but a drawer here is one who draws, and the top ones are Royal Academicians.
explanation.definitionFit: A commercial traveller is a travelling salesman who visits customers to take orders.

clue.text: Something loopy and irrational about religious books

parts.note: pi is the best-known irrational number
c, for circa, means about
OT is the Old Testament, a collection of religious books

explanation.surface: Someone is dismissing a crazy, irrational attitude to scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loopy' and 'irrational' both look like 'mad'; in fact one defines a looped thing and the other is a number.
explanation.definitionFit: A picot is a small decorative loop of thread along the edge of lace or ribbon, so literally a loopy item.

clue.text: Verse work recalled English essay

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the letters come back the other way

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a musical work
E is the standard abbreviation for English
an essay is an attempt, a try

explanation.surface: A student remembers a poem studied alongside an English essay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essay' is not a school composition but its older sense, an attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Verse and poetry are synonyms for literature written in metre and lines.

clue.text: Game starts in confusion, opening once, and never finishing

indicators.note: not finishing means stopping short, so the final letter is dropped
a start is where something begins, so each word is cut down to its first letter

parts.note: first letter
first letter
the word without its last letter
the word without its last letter

explanation.surface: A game that begins chaotically and, once under way, never ends.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicators are shared: 'starts in' covers two words and 'never finishing' covers the two after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooncan is an old two-player card game of the rummy family, so it is a specific example of a game.

clue.text: Hint for one? Dunce needs to have 3!

indicators.note: the answer at 3 down means got up, and in a down entry going up means reading from the bottom

parts.note: a nit, or nitwit, is a fool
e.g. means for example, for one

explanation.surface: A cheeky aside: a hint, for example, is what a dunce needs.
explanation.walkthrough: The 3 refers to 3 down, whose meaning, got up, is the instruction. Both short pieces are turned upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinge is a slight trace of colour or quality, so a small suggestion, as a noun.

clue.text: One who composed message on Mother's Day gift? Revolting, oily stuff!

parts.note: Alban Berg was an Austrian composer

indicators.note: a revolt is a turning over, so the letters are overturned and read the other way

parts.note: a present for a mother might carry the tag 'To Ma'

explanation.surface: Someone writes a card for Mum's present and finds it disgusting and greasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One who composed message' looks like the card writer, but the break comes after 'composed': a composer, then the message.
explanation.definitionFit: Bergamot oil, pressed from the rind of a citrus fruit, flavours Earl Grey tea and scents perfumes.

clue.text: Plant, end of stem becoming black, declined

indicators.note: one thing becoming another means it is swapped for it, so a letter is replaced

parts.note: to plant something is to embed it

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: its last letter, which is swapped out
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A gardener describes a plant wilting as its stem blackens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a noun in the garden picture, but it is the verb meaning embed; its M becomes B.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebbed describes something receding or diminishing, like a falling tide, so it matches a past-tense verb meaning waned.

clue.text: Quilt stuffing placed on rock for makeshift bed

parts.note: to rock something is to shake it
down is the soft feather filling of a duvet

explanation.surface: A camper spreads a duvet filling on a rock as an improvised bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' looks like a stone to lie on, but it is the verb meaning sway.
explanation.definitionFit: A shakedown is an old term for a temporary bed made up on the floor or on straw.

clue.text: Love to come together briefly to spin a little mischief!

indicators.note: said briefly, a word is cut short, losing its final letter
spinning round makes something face the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: love is a zero score, nil
merge, trimmed of its final E

explanation.surface: Lovers meeting for a quick dance get up to a bit of harmless mischief.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole string, not just the last piece, is turned round. 'Love' is the tennis score nil.
explanation.definitionFit: A gremlin is an imaginary small sprite blamed for mechanical faults, so a tiny embodiment of mischief.

clue.text: Complaint harboured by Anthea on meeting Rachel

indicators.note: what is harboured is sheltered deep inside, so only the tucked-away inner run of letters is kept and the outside is discarded

parts.note: the tail of the name, with its front removed
the name without its final letter

explanation.surface: Anthea nurses a grievance when she runs into Rachel.
explanation.walkthrough: This works like a hidden word: 'on meeting' tells you to push the two names together, and the letters then sit inside the join.
explanation.definitionFit: Complaint here is the medical sense, an ailment, and pain in the ear is one such ailment.

clue.text: Baked small crumbles for function

indicators.note: whatever crumbles breaks into bits that can be put back in another order

parts.note: taken letter for letter
taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A small baked treat falls apart when served at an event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crumbles' looks like a pudding, a British baked fruit dessert, but it is a verb telling you to break the letters up.
explanation.definitionFit: A function is a formal social gathering, and a masquerade dance where guests wear masks is one.

clue.text: Shower cap placed around heated bath

indicators.note: what is placed around something surrounds it, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: to cap a story is to better it
a spa is a hot bath or thermal spring

explanation.surface: Someone puts on a shower cap around a hot bath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shower cap' reads as one bathroom item, but 'Shower' is the definition, a verb, and 'cap' means outdo.
explanation.definitionFit: To bespatter is to splash or spray something with drops, so it is a verb meaning to shower.

clue.text: Girl falling just short of the record?

indicators.note: falling just short means ending slightly early, so the final letter goes

parts.note: an annal is a record of one year's events

explanation.surface: A girl narrowly misses breaking the record.
explanation.walkthrough: The singular annal, usually met only in the plural annals, is one historical record.
explanation.definitionFit: Anna is a common female first name, the usual crossword sense of a girl.

clue.text: Social worker getting one's child to stop going on slide

parts.note: an ant is a worker in a social insect colony
I is one, so one's is I'S
a kid is a child

explanation.surface: A social worker takes a child off a playground slide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' is not a council caseworker but an insect living in a colony; the definition phrase describes purpose, as anti-skid tyres or surfaces do.
explanation.definitionFit: Anti-skid describes something designed to prevent slipping, such as treads or mats, which is its purpose.

clue.text: Maybe wanting fare controlled by US bank

parts.note: what is under someone is controlled by them
the Fed is the Federal Reserve, the American central bank

explanation.surface: Someone after a bus fare might be governed by an American bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fare' suggests a ticket price, but it means food; 'Maybe' allows that underfed is only one way of lacking it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone underfed has too little to eat, so they are lacking food, which is fare in its dining sense.

clue.text: Soft food in time something that flies mysteriously rebuffed?

parts.note: T is the standard abbreviation for time

indicators.note: a rebuff sends someone back, so the letters are sent back the other way

parts.note: an unidentified flying object

explanation.surface: A mysterious flying object is shooed off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is only a link here, not a container signal: the pieces simply sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Tofu is bean curd, a soft, pale food made from pressed soya milk.

clue.text: Having left later, dallies with Yankee in front of others

indicators.note: a letter that has left its place and turns up later means the order is disturbed

parts.note: to dally is to flirt
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone leaves late, flirting with an American along the way.
explanation.walkthrough: As printed the clue is faulty: moving L later is not enough, as T must move too. The Times later corrected it to 'Flirts outrageously with Yankee'.
explanation.definitionFit: Firstly means in the first place, ahead of the rest, as an adverb of order.

clue.text: Harsh call by the way to split a medical department

indicators.note: splitting something opens a gap in it where another piece can go

parts.note: taken as written
St is short for street, a way
to ring someone is to call them
ENT is ear, nose and throat, a hospital department

explanation.surface: A doctor makes a curt phone call in passing, splitting up a hospital unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' puts the way beside the call, making one block that then goes inside A plus ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Astringent criticism is severe and biting, so the adjective shares the sense of sharp and unkind.

clue.text: Self-promotion developed fully, with energy rising

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means climbing to the top, so a bottom letter moves to the front

parts.note: to develop a thing, like a cold, is to get it
fully grown fruit is ripe
E, the physics symbol for energy, is already the final letter of the previous piece; this names the letter that moves

explanation.surface: A fully developed ego keeps getting more energetic about promoting itself.
explanation.walkthrough: Developed fully reads as the phrase 'got ripe'; its final E, the symbol for energy, climbs to the top of this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An ego trip is an activity done mainly to boost one's own importance, so vain self-aggrandisement.

clue.text: Cooper? In short, one thing that coops

indicators.note: putting it in short means cutting it down, so the last letter is lost

parts.note: Henry Cooper was a much-loved British heavyweight boxer
un is French for one

explanation.surface: Asks whether a cooper, or anything else, makes coops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooper' looks like a trade, a barrel-maker, but it is the boxer Henry Cooper, a household name in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen run is an enclosure keeping poultry penned in, so it confines them as a coop does.

clue.text: There's word of action every so often being at plant

parts.note: a verb is a doing word

indicators.note: something happening every so often occurs at intervals, so only spaced-out letters count

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Someone notes that there's an occasional call to action being made at a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' could be a factory in the surface; here it is the definition, a garden flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbena is a genus of flowering garden plants, also called vervain, so it is one example.

clue.text: Sex with a dish

parts.note: sex is Latin for six, VI in Roman numerals
and means with, joining things together

explanation.surface: A racy menu pairing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sex' is the Latin number six, not the act.
explanation.definitionFit: A viand is an old word for an item of food, especially a choice one served at table.

clue.text: West Ham's football stars making international European team

indicators.note: West Ham is in East London, where Cockney speech drops an H, so a leading H vanishes

parts.note: the FA is the Football Association
stars are heroes

explanation.surface: West Ham United's star players get picked for an international European side.
explanation.walkthrough: West Ham is a London football club, and Londoners of the East End famously drop their H's, so heroes becomes 'eroes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Faeroe Islands, a North Atlantic territory, field their own national football side in European competitions.

clue.text: Drive off after payment picked up for shawl

indicators.note: to pick up a signal is to hear it, so the sound matters, not the spelling

parts.note: a fee is a payment
to shoo is to drive away

explanation.surface: A driver speeds off after paying, collecting a scarf on the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' reverses the order of the clue: the payment sound comes first. A fichu is pronounced fee-shoo.
explanation.definitionFit: A fichu is a small triangular scarf worn over a woman's shoulders and neck, a kind of wrap.

clue.text: A new strategy for crossing river in inhospitable territory

indicators.note: to cross something is to span it, so one piece stretches over and around another

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
a tactic is a plan or strategy
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Explorers devise a fresh plan for fording a river in hostile country.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all expedition planning; 'crossing' is not fording but wrapping round.
explanation.definitionFit: The Antarctic is the frozen polar region around the South Pole, famously hostile to life.

clue.text: Physicist backing Whistler's claim?

indicators.note: going backing means moving backwards, so the letters are read from the end

parts.note: someone with a whistle might say 'I'm ref', claiming to be the referee

explanation.surface: A scientist supports the painter Whistler's assertion.
explanation.walkthrough: Whistler looks like James McNeill Whistler, the painter; the question mark says it is just someone blowing a whistle, a referee.
explanation.definitionFit: Enrico Fermi was an Italian-American Nobel laureate who built the first nuclear reactor.

clue.text: Party before long for senior member

parts.note: a do is a party
to long for something is to yen for it

explanation.surface: A party elder is waiting to take their seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' is a verb meaning yearn, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A doyen is the most respected or longest-serving person in a group or profession.

clue.text: Drinks at college assembly

parts.note: a round is a set of drinks bought for a group
a student at university is said to be up

explanation.surface: Students have drinks together at a college gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'up' at Oxford or Cambridge means studying there, a British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A round-up is a gathering together of people or animals, such as cattle, in one place.
